subject: mathematics
question_text: In △ABC, show that (b − c)² cos²(A/2) + (b + c)² sin²(A/2) = a².

mark_split.label: Use cos A and the cosine rule

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each standard result you use and the order you use them in.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Expand and group the squares
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. Group on b² + c² and on 2bc: the first bracket is 1, the second is the double-angle form.
steps.memory_tip: Group on b² + c² and on 2bc — the first bracket is cos² + sin² = 1, the second is the double-angle form.

recall.must_convey: That expanding both squares and grouping gives (b²+c²)(cos² + sin²) + 2bc(sin² − cos²).
accept: expand both squares and collect the b squared plus c squared and the two b c separately
the first bracket is cos squared plus sin squared which is one
the two b c bracket has sin squared minus cos squared
rendu squares expand chesi b square plus c square ni separate ga theeyali
group the common part and the two b c part

steps.why: Both squares share b² + c² and differ only in the sign of 2bc. Grouping on that split makes one bracket the Pythagorean identity and the other the double-angle form.
common_mistakes: Grouping so that the 2bc bracket keeps the cosine first and the sign is reversed.

steps.label: Use cos A and the cosine rule
steps.margin_note: The other mark. cos²(A/2) − sin²(A/2) is cos A, and b² + c² − 2bc cos A is the cosine rule for a².
steps.memory_tip: cos²θ − sin²θ = cos 2θ, so with θ = A/2 the bracket is cos A and the line becomes the cosine rule.

recall.must_convey: That cos²(A/2) − sin²(A/2) = cos A, leaving b² + c² − 2bc cos A, which is a² by the cosine rule.
accept: cos squared minus sin squared is cos of double the angle so it is cos A
what is left is b squared plus c squared minus two b c cos A
that is the cosine rule so it equals a squared
cos square minus sin square ante cos A, adi cosine rule
the last line is the cosine rule written backwards

steps.why: cos²θ − sin²θ = cos 2θ with θ = A/2 gives cos A, and what is left is exactly the cosine rule read from right to left.
common_mistakes: Using a² = b² + c² + 2bc cosA with the wrong sign.
